Secrets and payloads are never stored; results are deterministic so confidence is always 1.0.

listing.shortDescription: Build a signed webhook envelope + ready-to-send request for Stripe, GitHub, Shopify, Slack, Svix, or generic HMAC
listing.description: Agent-native signed-webhook envelope builder computed with real cryptography (Node crypto HMAC), not a language model. /build takes a provider preset, an event_type, the payload data, and a signing secret, then serializes a canonical {id,type,created,data} JSON body, computes the HMAC signature, and returns the provider-formatted signature header(s), the timestamp and idempotency message id used, the exact signed string, and a complete ready-to-send request spec (method, url, headers, body). Supports Stripe (t=…,v1=…), GitHub (sha256=…), Shopify (base64), Slack (v0:ts:body), Svix/standard-webhooks (id.ts.body), and generic HMAC. Ideal for integration tests, replays, fixtures, and local development. The one-call /lookup adds a reasoning object and send guidance. Results are deterministic so confidence is always 1.0; secrets are never stored.

info.title: Webhook Payload Builder API
info.description: Deterministic signed-webhook envelope builder. Given an event type, payload data, and a signing secret, it serializes a canonical {id,type,created,data} JSON body, computes a real HMAC signature, and returns the provider-formatted signature header(s), timestamp, idempotency id, and a ready-to-send request spec for Stripe, GitHub, Shopify, Slack, Svix/standard-webhooks, or generic HMAC. Perfect for tests, replays, and local development. Real cryptography, never an LLM guess; confidence is always 1.0. Secrets are never stored.

HeaderMap.description: HTTP header name → value. Names vary by provider.

url.description: Target URL if you supplied one, else null.

body.description: Raw body to send verbatim (the exact bytes that were signed).

signature.description: The signature value with provider prefix.

signed_string.description: The exact string that was HMAC-signed.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds used in the signature (supplied or generated).

message_id.description: Event/message id used for idempotency (supplied or generated).

secret_echoed.description: Always false — the signing secret is used to sign and then discarded; it is never returned or stored.

data.description: The event payload data (placed under envelope.data).

secret.description: Signing secret. Svix accepts a "whsec_" base64 secret.

timestamp.description: Optional unix-seconds timestamp; generated if omitted.

message_id.description: Optional event/message id; generated if omitted.

url.description: Optional target URL echoed into the request spec.

reasoning.why_result_generated: Serialized a canonical {id,type,created,data} envelope, built the Stripe signed string (HMAC-SHA256 over "{timestamp}.{raw_body}", hex; header is "t=<ts>,v1=<sig>".), and computed HMAC-sha256 (hex).
key_factors: Signed string shape: HMAC-SHA256 over "{timestamp}.{raw_body}", hex; header is "t=<ts>,v1=<sig>".
invalidators: Changing the body bytes (whitespace, key order, re-encoding) invalidates the signature.
The receiver must use the same secret and verify over the raw body.
Timestamped schemes also fail if the receiver enforces a tolerance and the timestamp is stale.
